question: Assume today is 2026-09-10. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total container volume handled by the Port of Los Angeles in September 2026, in TEUs (twenty-foot equivalent units; loaded and empty imports and exports combined), as it will be first reported in the Port of Los Angeles's monthly cargo news release.

target.what: Total container volume handled by the Port of Los Angeles (loaded + empty, imports + exports combined) as first reported in the Port's monthly cargo news release for September 2026
target.publisher: Port of Los Angeles (Port of Los Angeles monthly cargo news release / TEU statistics)
target.caveats: Target period is future relative to cutoff (2026-09-10); only ~10 days of September will have elapsed at cutoff, so most of the month must be forecast. Definition is total TEU (loaded imports + loaded exports + empty imports + empty exports), matching the Port's headline 'total TEU' figure. Alternat

p1.role: Port of Los Angeles total TEU, September 2025

methods.rationale: Year-on-year scaling of last September's actual total by a change factor grounded in 2026 YTD growth, July 2026 YoY decline, and the Port's FY forecast. Shared dependency: relies on p1 being the correct September 2025 baseline.

p53.role: Port of Los Angeles total TEU, July 2026 (latest actual month)

a2.role: September/August seasonal ratio applied as a two-month step from July

methods.rationale: Anchors on the latest actual month (July 2026, 960,464) and applies a seasonal step to September. Uses p53 as the most recent observed level; a2 captures the typical July-to-September decline. Failure mode: if August 2026 deviates sharply from July, this misstates the base.

Uses the target's own monthly history (2025 full year plus July 2026) to project September 2026 via seasonal/trend extrapolation. Requires last September's value (p1) and a recent month (p53); captures seasonality and recent softening.

assumptions.name: September 2026 / September 2025 total TEU change factor
assumptions.rationale: 2026 YTD through July is +1.8% vs 2025, but July 2026 was -5.8% YoY and the Port forecasts a 7% FY2026-27 decline; September 2025 was already a weak month (883k, -7.5%), so a modest further decline is plausible. Range spans flat to -15%.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 follows the recent soft YoY trend rather than a sharp rebound.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a strong September 2026 peak-season surge or a collapse beyond -15%.

assumptions.name: September/August seasonal ratio adjustment
assumptions.rationale: Historically September is slightly below August (2025: 883/958=0.92; 2024: 955/961=0.99; 2023: 748/828=0.90); a mild post-peak decline is typical.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of an unusual September surge or collapse relative to August.

assessment.note: Port of Los Angeles September totals for 2025, 2024, 2023 from the same publisher's monthly cargo releases; consistent definition (loaded+empty, imports+exports). These are the core seasonal anchors for a September forecast. p1 (883,053) is the most recent September and the base for a year-over-year route.

August totals for 2025/2024/2023; together with the September values they define the historical September/August ratio (~0.92 in 2025, ~0.99 in 2024, ~0.90 in 2023). Same source and definition, so they corroborate the seasonal step but are not independent of p1/p38/p68.

July 2026 total of 960,464 TEU appears identically in the Port's own release (p53/p219/p233), a news summary (p118), and Spanish-language trade press (p258/p260). These are copies of one measurement, not independent confirmations; they establish the latest actual level and the -5.8% y/y July change.

July 2026 component breakdown (loaded imports 499,552; loaded exports 111,776; empties 349,137) repeated across sources. Internally consistent (imports+exports=611,327 loaded; +empties=960,464). Useful for structure but redundant copies.

Jan–Jul 2026 cumulative 6,083,067 TEU vs 5,975,649 in 2025 (+1.8%). Same underlying Port statistic repeated; establishes that 2026 YTD is slightly ahead of 2025 despite a weak July, implying strong H1 front-loading.

Port leadership guidance: 7% decline forecast for FY2026-27 (p103/p104), Q1 2026 weakness (p121/p122), January import/export declines (p124/p125). methods.rationale: Year-over-year route anchored on the most recent September actual (p1), adjusted by a change factor grounded in the Port's own FY2026-27 guidance (p103/p104), Q1 weakness (p121/p122), and the July 2026 y/y decline (p53 vs p3). p53.role: Port of Los Angeles total TEU, July 2026 (latest actual month)

methods.rationale: Seasonal-step route from the latest actual month (July 2026, p53) using the historical September/July ratio. The ratio is derived from kept September and July values (p1/p3, p38/p40, p68/p71) but encoded as an assumption because the library has no ratio-of-two-months method; the assumption's range reflects the dispersion of those historical ratios. Failure mode: if 2026's seasonal shape differs materially from 2023–2025.

Own-history route using the 13 consecutive monthly totals from January 2025 through July 2026 (p7–p6 plus p53). With 13+ months the library averages AutoETS, Theta, a y/y growth estimate and a global model, capturing both seasonality and the recent softening. Shared dependency: p1 and p3 also feed m1/m2, so this is not an independent route.

assumptions.name: September 2026 / September 2025 total TEU change factor
assumptions.rationale: Port leadership forecast a 7% decline for FY2026-27 (p103/p104) and reported Q1 2026 weakness (p121/p122); July 2026 was -5.8% y/y (p53 vs p3) while Jan–Jul 2026 was +1.8% (p59 vs p60), implying H1 front-loading that fades in H2. September 2025 (p1) was itself a soft month (-7.5% y/y), so a further modest decline is plausible; range spans flat-to-strongly-down.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 behaves like the H2 2026 trend implied by the Port's own guidance and July's y/y decline.
assumptions.falsified_by: August 2026 LA volume reported well above 2025 August, or national import data showing a renewed peak-season surge.

assumptions.name: September 2026 / July 2026 seasonal step factor
assumptions.rationale: Historical September/July ratios at LA: 2025 883,053/1,019,837≈0.87; 2024 954,706/939,600≈1.02; 2023 748,440/684,291≈1.09. The 2024/2023 values were distorted by front-loading and recovery; the 2025 ratio (~0.87) is the cleanest recent seasonal step. A value near 0.90 with a wide range reflects this dispersion.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 follows a normal post-peak seasonal decline from July 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of an unusual late-2026 demand surge or port disruption shifting the seasonal pattern.

methods.label: m3
methods.rationale: Own-history route using the 13 consecutive monthly totals from January 2025 through July 2026 (p7–p6 plus p53). With 13+ months the library averages AutoETS, Theta, a y/y growth estimate and a global model, capturing both seasonality and the recent softening. Shared dependency: p1 and p3 also feed m1/m2, so this is not an independent route.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
